text:
maya: Manual DNS failover initiated to us-west-2 at 2025-08-12T11:24Z. EU prod nodes lost heartbeat -> routing failures. Switched primary A record to us-west via Route53 failover set-id rr-usw-1. TTL temporarily set to 60s. @sam @josh
ops-bot: incident created: INCIDENT-20250812-23 DNS failover (eu-central -> us-west). Severity: P1.
sam: Why TTL 60? We normally set 30s for failovers to minimize stale caches.
maya: Console was flaky and API timed out, couldn't push 30 so set 60 quickly via console. Change-id: C12345.
josh: Edge/CDN caches still resolving eu IPs from some ISPs. Quick dig from 8.8.8.8 shows eu exit IPs: 
```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-inference.com A
34.200.12.5
34.200.12.5
```
Those map to eu egress pool, so client requests still hitting eu POPs.
elena: Fastly shows cached host entries with cache-control=300; I submitted purge (ticket #FAST-789). They acknowledged — propagation estimate 5-10m.
network-bot: BGP note: us-west announce injected, but some IX/peers still prefer eu next-hops due to older path prepends. BGP convergence estimate 6-12 minutes.
sam: So root causes = resolver TTL + CDN cache-control + BGP path preference. All three add latency to failover. Pre-failover TTL reduction would've helped. Post-mortem item.
maya: Interim workaround: applied weighted routing 80% us-west / 20% eu to gradually shift traffic. Applied via change-batch (aws change-id C12346). Hoping that gradual shift reduces 5xxs while caches flip.
josh: Did a `dig +trace` — some resolvers hit parent NS with long SOA/refresh TTLs: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16 <<>> api.redwood-inference.com A +trace
;; Received 192.0.2.1#53 from 198.51.100.1
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
redwood-inference.com. 3600 IN SOA ns-1.route53.net. hostmaster.redwood 2025081201 7200 900 1209600 3600
```
SOA refresh/TTL on parent zone is 3600, causing some recursive resolvers to stick.
sam: Parent delegation TTLs are sometimes outside our control (registrar/registry). Add a runbook step to verify parent TTLs for critical zones before maintenance.
maya: Status update: majority of traffic now shifted, error rate down from ~35% to ~2%. Some EU customers still see degraded latency due to BGP pathing and CDN edge staleness. CDN purge in progress.
elena: Follow-ups: request to add automated Route53 health checks with lower failover TTLs, pre-warm us-west capacity earlier, and add explicit playbook step: "lower Route53 TTL to 30 and issue CDN purge at least 10m before failover".
sam: Cost implication: pre-warming and cross-region burst will increase egress/reserved capacity costs — need finance signoff for >10% additional mitigation budget.
maya: After-action checklist: 
- [ ] Postmortem with timeline and root causes
- [ ] Update ops playbook: minimum TTLs, weighted shift pattern for failovers
- [ ] Add monitoring alert: "DNS skew between authoritative records and edge POPs"
- [ ] Registrar escalation contact added to critical zone docs
ops-bot: incident resolved: STATUS=mitigated, follow-up required. Duration=00:24:34.
network-bot: Final BGP convergence logged at 2025-08-12T11:44Z.
maya: Thanks all — I'll start the postmortem draft and tag owners for the checklist items.
